overview: Two of the most commonly isolated Enterobacterales in clinical labs, distinguished mainly by motility and capsule.
genZNote: Both Enterobacterales, only one bothers to move.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A motile, lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rod and the most common cause of community-acquired UTIs.
aspects.valueB: A non-motile, heavily encapsulated, lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rod associated with mucoid colonies.

aspects.label: Capsule
aspects.valueA: Thin or absent capsule in most strains.
aspects.valueB: Prominent polysaccharide capsule, producing large, mucoid, sticky colonies.

aspects.label: Clinical Associations
aspects.valueA: Leading cause of UTIs, and a common cause of neonatal meningitis and gram-negative bacteremia.
aspects.valueB: Associated with hospital-acquired pneumonia, UTIs, and liver abscesses, especially in diabetics and hospitalized patients.

aspects.label: Antibiotic Resistance Concern
aspects.valueA: ESBL and carbapenem-resistant strains exist but are less dominant globally than in Klebsiella.
aspects.valueB: A major reservoir for ESBL and carbapenemase (e.g. KPC) genes, driving multidrug-resistant outbreaks in hospitals.
